{"rule":"Return this JSON object with the rule field unchanged and, in the text field, an original fictional passage of about 250 words that comes immediately AFTER the current text in the same invented story.","text":"Mara counted the ticks. One, two, three—then the watch stopped.

The woman in yellow had vanished. Only the empty basket bobbed against a bridge pier, turning slowly in the current.

Tomas let go of Mara’s sleeve. “We should find the tower.”

“Which tower?”

He pointed beyond the rooftops. The town’s old bell tower rose above the square, though Mara was certain it had been shorter that morning. Its top disappeared into a ragged veil of cloud. A light glimmered behind one narrow window.

They crossed the bridge together. At the far end, a child stood beside a lamppost, holding a paper boat. Mara recognized him from the reflection: his coat was too long, his hair too neat. He looked at the watch in her hand.

“It’s broken,” she said.

“No,” the child replied. “It’s waiting.”

He set the boat in a puddle. Instead of drifting toward the gutter, it slid uphill, toward the tower. The child followed it, glancing back only once.

Tomas’s face had gone pale. “That’s the way we came out.”

Mara looked down at the watch. A new mark had appeared on its blank face: a tiny door, drawn in silver. Beneath it, the hands began to move—not forward, but backward.

From somewhere above, the tower bell gave a muffled knock.

The paper boat vanished around the corner.

Mara closed her fingers around the watch. “If we go back, we go together.”

Tomas nodded. They followed the child’s trail through the rain-wet streets, while behind them the river kept running, dark and quick, beneath the bridge."}
